items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: this was, this was a rehearsal of Gil’s band plus Sting as a guest soloist

ctx.x: One of my favorite writers. I had one experience with him by the way, about a year before he died. This was the summer of ’87. It was a Monday morning and I was just lying in bed. The phone rings and I hear this voice at the other end of the phone, “This is Gil Evans,” who I’d never met before. He said, “Maria Schneider gave me your number. I’m doing a rehearsal this afternoon and I need a sub for Howard Johnson on baritone and bass clarinet. Can you do it? I’ll pay you.” And I resisted the temptation to say,…

this was, this was a rehearsal of Gil’s band plus Sting as a guest soloist, they were going to go to the Umbria Jazz Festival. So what we rehearsed was — Maria and Tom Malone had written some charts on Police tunes like “Synchronicity” and “Roxanne.” And they had a few charts in Gil’s book from that Jimi Hendrix album that he had done in the 70s. Those charts were not written by Gil by the way, they were by somebody else. And they were really not much, frankly. That album is not one of Gil’s great records. But…
Nice. I don’t think I would have —
